steps.observation: Work on this for 900 seconds; do not stop early. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Conceptual overview of a Transformer neural network

1. The problem it was designed to solve  
   Classical sequence models (RNNs, LSTMs) process tokens one-by-one. That makes it hard to (a) capture long-range dependencies and (b) use GPUs efficiently, because you cannot parallelize the time steps. The transformer replaces recurrence with attention so every token can look at every other token in a single step. That gives both better modeling of global context and vastly better parallelism.

2. Inputs become vectors with position information  
   • Tokenization converts text into discrete symbols (word pieces, BPE, etc.).  
   • Each token id is mapped to an embedding vector.  
   • Because attention itself is permutation-invariant, you add a position signal so the model can still tell order. The original paper adds fixed sinusoids; many modern variants learn position embeddings.

   The result after this step is a length-by-d_model matrix: one d-dimensional vector per token that “knows” its identity and its position.

3. Self-attention – how one token “looks” at the rest  
   At the heart of a transformer layer is the self-attention operation. Each input vector is linearly projected three different ways to produce a query Q, a key K, and a value V.  
   • The query says, “What am I looking for?”  
   • The keys of the other tokens say, “What do I contain?”  
   • Compatibility is the dot product Q·Kᵀ. After a softmax you get weights that sum to one. These weights are used to take a weighted average of the value vectors V. That average is the new, context-aware representation of the token.

   Because the softmax is computed over all tokens, every position can incorporate information from every other position in one hop, no matter how far apart they are.

4. Multi-head attention – different “subspaces” in parallel  
   Instead of one Q/K/V set, the projection is done h separate times with smaller dimensions (e.g., d_model = 768, h = 12 heads, each head size = 64). Each head can focus on different linguistic or semantic relations (subject-verb agreement, coreference, etc.). Afterwards the heads are concatenated and linearly recombined.

5. Feed-forward network (FFN) – token-wise nonlinearity  
   Following attention, each token’s vector passes through the same two-layer MLP: linear → ReLU/GELU → linear. Conceptually, attention mixes information across time; the FFN then mixes features within a position.

6. Residual connections and layer normalization  
   To stabilize deep stacks, transformers add the sub-layer output back to its input (a residual skip) and then apply LayerNorm. So each transformer block looks like:  
   a) x ← x + SelfAttention(x) ; x ← LayerNorm(x)  
   b) x ← x + FeedForward(x) ;    x ← LayerNorm(x)

7. Stacking layers  
   You stack N identical blocks (BERT-base uses 12, GPT-3 uses 96, etc.). Depth offers hierarchical abstraction; the first layers learn short-range patterns, higher ones unify broader context.

8. Decoder only, encoder only, encoder–decoder  
   • Encoder only (BERT): every layer is bi-directional self-attention; outputs are contextual token embeddings used for classification or masked-LM tasks.  
   • Decoder only (GPT): applies causal masks so a token only attends to earlier positions; outputs feed directly to a softmax to predict the next token.  
   • Encoder–decoder (original Transformer, T5): encoder produces a source sequence representation; the decoder attends to both its own past (causal) and the encoder output to generate targets (e.g., translation).

9. Training objectives  
   • Masked language modeling (BERT): randomly hide 15 % of tokens and have the model fill them in.  
   • Autoregressive next-token prediction (GPT): predict each token given all prior ones.  
   • Sequence-to-sequence cross-entropy (translation, summarization): train decoder to emit gold target sequence given source.

10. Why attention is powerful  
    • Direct access: Any token can attend to anything else without repeated steps.  
    • Interpretability: Attention weights can sometimes be inspected to see which words influenced a prediction.  
    • Differentiable lookup: It’s like letting the model build task-specific weighted averages of the entire sequence on the fly.

11. Computational characteristics  
    • Complexity is O(n²) in sequence length due to the all-pairs dot products, which is why long-sequence variants (Longformer, Performer, etc.) try to approximate or sparsify attention.  
    • Everything inside a layer is matrix multiplication, making GPUs/TPUs happy.

12. Intuition recap  
    Think of each token sending out a questionnaire (query) to every other token’s résumé (key) and collecting tailored notes (value). Multi-head means you have several different questionnaires simultaneously. The resulting augmented token descriptions are then polished by a small MLP, and the whole procedure repeats in deeper layers, gradually building rich, context-aware meanings that are useful for downstream language tasks.

By replacing recurrence with attention, transformers achieve both better language understanding and the ability to scale to billions of parameters using modern hardware.
